text:
nina: FYI new hire hit a weird hang in the onboarding sample when doing pagination + client-side throttling. Looks like backpressure from retries is preventing the paginator from making progress.

carl: ugh, onboarding flakes are the worst. Which sample / SDK version?

nina: node quickstart, bundled @redwood/sdk-js v0.7.0. Command: `npm run sample -- --pageSize=250 --concurrency=6`. After a couple of 429s the streamer goes silent for ~25-40s, then resumes. Repro on mac and in CI.

hamid: logs? Curious if x-retry-after is being respected or if the client fallback is too aggressive.

nina: pasted logs (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-28T18:22:01Z] INFO paginator: start page=4
[2026-03-28T18:22:01Z] WARN api: 429 rate_limit (x-retry-after=1)
[2026-03-28T18:22:01Z] INFO throttle: token-bucket drained tokens=0
[2026-03-28T18:22:01Z] INFO retry: sleeping 1000ms attempt=1
[2026-03-28T18:22:02Z] INFO throttle: refill +1 (tokens=1)
[2026-03-28T18:22:32Z] INFO paginator: no worker active, awaiting lease
```

nnnina: The odd bit is refill happens quickly but paginator doesn't schedule workers until much later. Looks like workers are waiting for a multi-token lease or a semaphore held by a failed retry.

hamid: That matches an issue we saw in 0.7 where the token-bucket was shared globally and the paginator code tried to reserve N tokens per page. If many pages request at once, they all block until enough tokens accumulate -> long stalls.
carl: Did we document this in onboarding? New hires assume it's a backend outage. We should be explicit.

sdk-bot: Created issue RD-5298: "sample: paginator stalls under client-side token-bucket semantics in sdk-js <0.8" https://redwood/issue/RD-5298

hamid: Quick mitigation options: 1) bump sample dependency to >=0.8 which uses per-request permits + jitter; 2) change sample defaults to concurrency=2 and pageSize=100; 3) change ThrottleConfig in sample to allow small burst and faster refill.
nina: I'd prefer bumping SDK in the sample so new hires get the improved defaults. But that might hide subtle production regressions customers see with older SDKs.
carl: Good point. For onboarding, bump sample to ^0.8 but add a README section "Why your app stalls: SDK parity and throttle semantics" that explains differences and shows ThrottleConfig examples. Also add a quick `scripts/heavy_paginate_repro.sh`.

hamid: Also recommend we add a small runtime check in sample: if bundled sdk < 0.8 warn the user with a one-liner suggesting upgrade or reduced concurrency. New hires often don't read changelogs.

sdk-bot: Task created RD-5299: "update samples: bump sdk, set conservative defaults, add repro + README note" https://redwood/tasks/RD-5299

nina: I'll open PR with: package update, set DEFAULT_PAGE_CONCURRENCY=2, add env REDWOOD_PAGINATOR_CONCURRENCY, include repro script, and a short warning if sdk version < 0.8.
carl: +1. Also add example ThrottleConfig snippets for dev/prod in README. Eg dev: {maxTokens:8,refillMs:200,jitter:true} prod: {maxTokens:64,refillMs:80,burst:8}.
hamid: one more caveat: ensure the sample respects x-retry-after header from the server. Some earlier client code ignored it and used exponential backoff only, which messes with token timing. Add an integration test that asserts retry delays respect the header when present.
nina: will add a tiny test that mocks a 429 with x-retry-after and asserts the client sleeps roughly that long.
devops-bot: Noted. We'll tag the samples release so quickstart images get rebuilt after PR merges.
sdk-bot: Linked RD-5298 and RD-5299 and added label "onboarding" to both.
nina: PR opened: https://redwood/pr/860 — bump to sdk-js ^0.8.1, default concurrency=2, added repro script + README note + version warning. Asking @hamid and @carl for quick review.
carl: reviewing now. tiny nit: use env var name REDWOOD_PAGINATOR_CONCURRENCY (consistency).
hamid: :+1: once merged, let's add a short playbook item in devex/playbooks: "If users report long pagination pauses: check SDK version, reduce paginator concurrency, or inspect x-retry-after in logs."
nina: will create the playbook entry after PR merges. Thanks folks.
